framework.name: National Core Arts Standards
framework.source: https://www.nationalartsstandards.org (the four artistic processes; wording is the school's own)

objectives.description: Use the elements of art, including line, shape, color, value and texture, to make a composition.
Generate ideas for an artwork through sketching, brainstorming and visual research.
Create a line drawing from observation using contour and gesture.
Use value and shading to show form in a still-life drawing.
Mix tints, shades and tones using a color wheel and use them in a painting.
Apply the principles of design, such as balance, contrast and emphasis, to a composition.
Create a work in a new medium, such as printmaking or clay, following safe procedures.
Prepare a finished work for display with a title, label and presentation.
Take part in a class critique by describing, analyzing and offering feedback on a peer's work.
Describe, analyze, interpret and evaluate a work by a historical or contemporary artist.
Compare the style of two artists and explain what makes each distinctive.
Explain how an artist's choices of materials affect the meaning of the work.
Describe how art reflects the culture and time in which it was made.
Make a work that responds to an issue or idea from another subject area.
Keep a sketchbook of daily drawings and reflect on your growth.
Revise a work after feedback and explain the changes you made.
Document your artwork with photographs and an artist statement.
Identify careers in the arts and the skills each requires.
Develop a body of work around a theme, with sketches that show your process.
Use linear perspective to create the illusion of space in a drawing.
Draw the human figure and face with accurate proportion.
Use composition techniques such as rule of thirds and a focal point to guide the viewer.
Paint with acrylic or watercolor using layering and glazing.
Work in a three-dimensional medium and consider the piece from all sides.
Experiment with mixed media and combine materials to express an idea.
Select, mount and display a group of works for an exhibition.
Write an artist statement that describes your intent and process.
Analyze how artists from different cultures use symbols and imagery.
Interpret the meaning of a contemporary artwork using evidence from the work.
Compare two artworks that address the same theme in different ways.
Research an art movement and explain how it responded to its historical context.
Describe how art can influence social or political ideas.
Create a work that takes a risk or begins with a mistake, and reflect on what you learned.
Give and receive critique in small groups using a shared vocabulary.
Maintain a sketchbook with weekly experiments and reflections.
Identify local arts opportunities, such as galleries, classes and public art.
Operate a digital camera using aperture, shutter speed and ISO and explain how they work together.
Use composition techniques such as the rule of thirds, leading lines and framing.
Control light by shooting in different conditions and using natural and artificial sources.
Photograph a subject from several angles and select the strongest image.
Use editing software to crop, adjust exposure and correct color.
Create a photo essay that tells a story in a series of images.
Shoot portraits and consider lighting, posing and the subject's comfort.
Prepare images for print and for the web at the right size and resolution.
Present a portfolio with titles and captions.
Take part in a critique and give feedback using a shared vocabulary.
Analyze the work of a documentary or fine art photographer and explain the choices.
Explain how an image can be altered and the ethical limits of editing.
Describe how photography has changed society, from photojournalism to social media.
Explain copyright and permissions for images and the rights of the people photographed.
Create a series on a theme such as place, identity or light.
Experiment with a technique such as long exposure, black and white, or macro.
Exhibit your work in a print or online show.
Explore careers in photography and visual communication.
Play assigned parts with accurate pitch, rhythm and tone on your instrument.
Perform major scales and arpeggios from memory in the keys required this quarter.
Sight-read a short passage at a steady tempo.
Follow the conductor's cues for tempo, dynamics and entrances.
Balance and blend your sound with the other players in your section.
Perform with correct posture, breath support and instrument care.
Compose or improvise a short melody using a given scale.
Arrange a simple phrase for your instrument by changing rhythm or dynamics.
Read and interpret key signatures, time signatures and musical terms.
Identify and describe the form of a piece of band music.
Evaluate a recording of the band's performance using a rubric.
Listen to a professional performance and compare it with ours.
Explain the history and style of a piece we are rehearsing.
Relate musical patterns to mathematics, such as fractions and ratios in rhythm.
Prepare for a concert, including a warm-up routine and a rehearsal plan.
Perform in marching band or pep band with correct formation and movement, as scheduled.
Keep a practice log and set goals for improvement.
Describe the role of music in your community and how you can take part in it.
Sing with correct posture, breath support and a healthy tone.
Warm up the voice with exercises for range, resonance and diction.
Sing your part in unison and in two-part harmony with accurate pitch.
Match pitch and blend with the section.
Follow a conductor's gestures for tempo, dynamics and cut-offs.
Sing a short solo or small-group part with confidence.
Perform songs in different languages with correct pronunciation.
Read simple notation, including key and time signatures, rhythm and solfege.
Sight-sing a short melodic pattern.
Describe the text, mood and style of a piece we are learning.
Evaluate a recording of the choir using a rubric and suggest improvements.
Create a short vocal improvisation or a new verse for a song.
Compose a four-bar melody for voice using a given scale.
Describe the history and cultural context of a piece in our repertoire.
Explain how singing connects with language, mathematics and wellness.
Prepare for a concert, including stage behavior and a performance plan.
Keep a practice log and set goals for your voice.
Identify community choirs and opportunities for continued singing.
Use improvisation to develop characters and scenes.
Create a character with a physical and vocal choice, a want and an obstacle.
Write a short scene with a beginning, middle and end.
Use voice, including volume, pace, articulation and emphasis, to communicate a character.
Use body, gesture and stage movement to communicate meaning.
Memorize and deliver a monologue with intention.
Rehearse and perform a scene with a partner, listening and responding in the moment.
Block a scene and use stage areas and terms such as upstage and downstage.
Plan a simple set, lighting or costume design for a scene.
Read a play and identify the plot, characters, conflict and theme.
Analyze a live or recorded performance and give evidence-based feedback.
Take part in a rehearsal critique, giving and receiving notes.
Describe the history of theater from ancient Greece to the present.
Explain how a play reflects the culture and time in which it was written.
Take on a production role such as stage manager, props or sound.
Adapt a short story or news event into a scene.
Prepare for a showcase and follow theater etiquette.
Identify careers in theater and community opportunities.
